subject: Animation
title: Lip Sync: Matching Mouth to Sound
description: Learn Lip Sync: Matching Mouth to Sound in one minute.

hook.text: Lip sync is the art of making an animated character's mouth match spoken words precisely and convincingly.

buildup.text: Animators break speech into phoneme shapes — the mouth positions for each sound in human language.

discovery.text: Only about eight to ten basic mouth shapes are needed to convincingly animate any English dialogue.

twist.text: Anime often uses simplified lip sync — just open and closed mouths — yet audiences barely notice the shortcut.

climax.text: Lip sync is the point where sound and image must be perfectly united, or the illusion of speech collapses.

punchline.text: Ten mouth shapes are enough to fake every word ever spoken.

quiz.question: How many basic mouth shapes are needed to animate convincing English dialogue?
options: About eight to ten phoneme shapes that cover all speech sounds
One open and one closed position
